summary: Shigeru Gorai (1908–1993) worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, later holding posts at Koyasan University, Kyoto Normal School, Otani University, Ryukoku University, and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore.
Shigeru Kato (1880–1946) was a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1900 to 1903 and later held a post there from circa 1925 to 1941.

Shigeru Matsumoto (1933–2010) was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1956) and Harvard University (~1963–1967). He held academic posts at Tenri University and the University of the Sacred Heart.
Shih-Hsiang Chen (1912–1971) was a sinologist who studied at Peking University from circa 1928 to 1932. He later held a post at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1945 to 1971.
Shikaripur N. Sridhar is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. At Stony Brook University, he served as Chair (attested 2007) and Director of the Center for India Studies (attested 2026).
Shikazo Mori (1906–1980) worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1926 to 1929 and held a post at Bukkyo University from circa 1970 to 1980.

Shikha Rajpurohit specializes in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College for Women (2009–2012) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (2014–2022), and was appointed Assistant Professor at Krea University in 2024.

Shili Xiong (1885–1968) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under Jian Ouyang at the China Institute of Inner Learning in 1920. He held posts at Peking University, Boone University, and Zhejiang University.

Shilpa Sumant is an Indologist who completed her Ph.D. at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (2000–2007). She held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 2009 and the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025).

Shimei Futabatei (1864–1909) worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Senshu College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Hitotsubashi University, and later held posts at the Army War College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Asahi Shimbun.

Shimin Geng (1929–2012) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China from circa 1949 to 1953 and held a post there from circa 1953 to 2000.

Shin Fujinaga (born 1958) works in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested in 1991 and 2000) and Hiroshima University (attested in 1992).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu (1889–1980) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Third Higher School and Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami, he held professorships at Hanazono, Ryukoku, Kyoto, Kyoto City University of Arts, and Harvard.

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga (1957–2022) specialized in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and held a professorship at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College, attested in 2015.

Shin'ya Yasutomi (1944–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and Otani University. He held academic posts at Otani University, the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute, and the Eastern Buddhist Society.

Shindai Sekiguchi (1907–1986) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from circa 1928 to 1934. He later served as a professor at Taisho University (~1964–1978) and Hanazono University (~1978–1984).

Shindo Kusumoto works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Kusumoto earned a PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shingen Takagi (born 1934) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku and Rissho universities under Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano, and held posts including Associate Professor and President at Koyasan University.

Shingo Einoo (born 1948) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau (~1977–1980) and held posts at the National Museum of Ethnology, University of Tokyo, and IOC.

Shinichi Nakazawa (born 1950) works in religious studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo from circa 1969 to 1977, he held posts at Chuo University, Tama Art University, and Meiji University.
